I have seen this behavior before, on rare occasions.
The first thing to do is to confirm that the part is a solid. Check Mass Properties to see if there is a volume.
If it does confirm as a solid body, the behavior is probably the result of some complex geometry at a single point on the model. Usually this is where 3 or more surfaces converge, or where there is a very small surface.
In either case, then next thing to try is to increase the model accuracy (smaller number). Any time you do this it will force a regeneration, which may cause some failures. Start with a small decrease of the value first. Whether anything fails or not, check the cross section and the drawing each time to see if you have resolved the issue.
If that doesn’t work, then I’m not sure what to suggest. You could try rolling back the part (insert mode) to see which feature the issue starts at. This might point you to the specific area of the part that is an issue.
Good luck, and please let us know how it goes.

subject: RE: PDM for Quantum
email_content:
**email: 1** 

 Hi Pavel,
Thanks for getting me set up with Windchill.
A few questions/queries maybe you could help with:
Say I have a part that is saved locally on my desktop or my OneDrive and I then save that file to my Windchill workspace. Is there then any link between that original file (on desktop or onedrive) and the one that lives in the Windchill workspace?
Usually the users are working locally, and not in OneDrive.  The local files and the checked in (commonspace) files do not have any connections, so you’re safe with the local modifications, and should only check in what you want and are ready with. You can keep all your files in your Workspace in the Workgroup Manager.
Is the ‘correct’ workflow for opening parts to do it through Windchill rather than file explorer or solidworks? Eg open my workspace, find the part, and click the ‘Open in SolidWorks’ icon?
****image018.png****
If the parts are inside of our Windchill and you want to work on them, than yes, those [arts should be opened through Windchill, since that’ll be your centralized repository.  Locally created files (inside your SolidWorks session) will also be inside your Workspace, and be labelled as “newly created”, which is that orange-ish circle or the “sun” as I’d like to call it😊.  You can then check them into our Windchill as well, like we triedwith that one part earlier.
When I open up the Documents > PTC Places > Workspace folder, it contains all the saved CAD files in the same place. Is the organisation of these parts into a folder structure something that I would do or would you guys need to create the folders for us?
****image019.png****
We can give you the power to create folders in your domain (Products) or we can manage that stuff for you, so you don’t have to think much about it and just request stuff.  With the team globally dispersed, I’d say giving one person the power to do this (on your time) will be the best way going forward.  That way you won’t have to wait on us.
I’d eventually like to upload some archive/reference assemblies (old designs of parts currently in service, which won’t change but need to be referenced for dimensions etc) to share with the US/Copenhagen teams. These assemblies have about 50-60 parts and they should be read-only for everyone except myself. What would be the best way to do this?
We can create a structure for some legacy stuff, like a container, where you are the only one with the Read/Write access, and therest of folks have Read-Only access.  Another way is to create a Library for global reference , and that way we can add other things like formats, etc.
How does your team handle the ‘tenting’ requirements for sensitive project designs given visibility of the files?
For us, we use CPMT tool, which is a centralized tool for our Surface and Xbox folks.  HoloLens, and Cloud teams don’t use it.  I think that tool is going through a journey of being updated to something that will be called CAMP.  If you have another way of tenting, I’d love to hear about it, and we can have your own process in place.
Could you please delete the CIRCCO part I uploaded during our meeting?
You got it!  Deleted😊I see you have 3 new objects in there!  Way to go and test this out!!
The system is working wonderfully for me, there’s practically zero lag so far. I can probably help him get set up if you create an account for him.
I just set Marjin up in Windchill and you can walk him through the Workgroup Manager setup (he doesn’t need to set up a PTC account if you can share the latest Workgroup Manager zip with him).  His username is marijnlucas and heis password is his Corpnet password😊.  Let’s see if he remembers his.

subject: RE: workspace update not updating objects but flagging them as updated
email_content:
**email: 1** 

 I have ran into several instances where workspace objects are not getting properly updated and current commenspace objects get overwritten (items are flagged as updated but the CAD data is not actually updated this allows checkout of a downrev part that will then overwrite changes made by someone else in commonspace).  This should not be possible.  I understand there are windchill settings that should control this and they appear to be set properly.  What am I missing here. Has this issue been reported by others.
****image001.png**** 


**email: 2** 

 Hello Andy,
This is a complex topic to discuss over email, but I will try to share what I know about Update.
If there are objects in a Workspace that are out of date, then Update will bring the latest Commonspace version in, replacing the out of date objects.
However, if there are out of date objects in a Workspace that have been modified by the user, Update will not overwrite these modified objects. Instead, it will update the metadata (Rev and version), allowing the user to then check these objects in as the latest version. I believe this is what you are encountering. While we have encountered this error in the past, I understand that this is how Windchill is supposed to function (protecting the users changes when using Update). We consider this to be a user error (incorrectly using Update).
For modified Workspace objects to be replaced by the latest Commonspace versions, the user must use Add To Workspace instead of Update. Add To Workspace will overwrite the user’s modified objects with the latest Commonspace version of the object.
I hope this helps. Please let us know if you would like to have a call on this. It is easier to explain in a conversation.
Regards,
Craig

(Starting off – I wasn’t clear on who was part of the original conversation on creating the ST10-KORE and ST10-JDM1 cabinets, so please add in relevant folks as needed. It seems like it might have been people who have since left MSFT.)
As you know we are sharing CAD with JDM1 by each having a different cabinet and controlling all parts in that cabinet. There are best practices on the KORE side that we would like to extend to JDM1 side, which I feel confident we can fix over time, as well as something time sensitive for Minos that is driving me to start this conversation now.
For the longer-term improvements, I’m curious to know how the JDM1 start parts were set up and why they might differ from our own standard start part.
if !supportLists1.endifWho would be the best people to include in the ongoing conversation of our shared best practices with JDM1?

if !supportLists2.endifWhat will be the best way to go about adding the missing relations in JDM1 parts to support KORE PCBA assembly drawing?

This new icon then launches Creo with the same settings as we employ internally at Microsoft. Realizing that some vendors will be uncomfortable launching an executable file that makes changes to their computers, there is also a manual process outlined in a slide deck. Rod can share more.
This process was only recently rolled out, so it is understandable that we have external users who are not using it yet. Updating parts and assemblies to comply with our standards is rather challenging, but I think that Rod can also help in this area.  PDMLink team,
I discussed this with Pavel earlier today, and I am following up here in email.
